original_idea: Um serviço de mentoria reversa para líderes de empresas tradicionais aprenderem sobre novas tecnologias e IA.
human_intent: Create a reverse‑mentorship service that pairs senior executives with junior technologists so leaders can learn about new tech and AI directly from those on the front lines.
refined_idea: Pair each senior leader with a junior employee (or external expert) who acts as a mentor on a scheduled basis (e.g., weekly 1‑hour sessions) to discuss recent developments, use‑cases, and strategic implications of emerging technologies and AI.
what_changed: Nova opção: Traditional executive training programs (workshops, seminars, MOOCs) delivered by external vendors.
Nova opção: Hiring external consultants to advise leaders on technology strategy.
Nova opção: Internal innovation labs where leaders observe pilot projects.

critique.vulnerability: Resistance from senior leaders who may view reverse mentorship as a threat to authority
critique.why_it_matters: Can lead to low participation and undermine the program’s credibility

critique.vulnerability: Overburdening junior mentors with additional responsibilities
critique.why_it_matters: May reduce their productivity and lead to burnout

critique.vulnerability: Potential leakage of confidential strategic information
critique.why_it_matters: Could expose the company to competitive risk

assumptions: Senior executives are open to being mentored by junior staff
Junior mentors have sufficient expertise and communication skills
The organization will allocate time for mentorship sessions
Confidentiality and trust can be maintained
Mentorship will lead to actionable insights for the leader
uncertainties: Legal liability for advice given during sessions
Cultural fit in highly hierarchical organizations
How to match mentors and mentees based on industry relevance and personality fit
Compensation or recognition model for junior mentors
Optimal frequency and duration of sessions

Ponto de decisão humana: Selection of mentor‑mentee pairings, determination of compensation/reward structures for junior mentors, and definition of success criteria require normative decisions aligned with company values and culture.

candidate_possibilities.mechanism: Traditional executive training programs (workshops, seminars, MOOCs) delivered by external vendors.
Hiring external consultants to advise leaders on technology strategy.
candidate_possibilities.justification: Consulting is a well‑known route for expertise acquisition.
tradeoffs: Expensive, may lack internal knowledge transfer

candidate_possibilities.mechanism: Internal innovation labs where leaders observe pilot projects.
candidate_possibilities.justification: Leaders can learn by observing internal experiments.
tradeoffs: Leaders may not get focused, one‑on‑one guidance
